synthesis: DEV-2575 reports that Scout field users who forget their email have no recovery path, and admins cannot reset passwords on their behalf. VERIFIED: Scout PWA uses email+password auth (Login.vue → ClarityScoutAuthController:21-87); Clarity main panel uses OTP/passwordless (CustomLoginPage → OneTimePassword, prior Clarity OTP work). Scout has NO forgot-password / password-reset routes or controllers (web.php:104-113 has only set-password for onboarding, force-login for admin impersonation). Admin resend_onboarding action (ScoutUsersResource:356-412) ONLY works when email_verified_at IS NULL (line 368), so it covers pre-onboarding only — once a user has set their password and verified, that button disappears and there is no fallback. The ticket proposes two solutions: (A) admin-side password reset / send recovery link from admin panel, (B) magic-link / passwordless auth like Clarity (PREFERRED). AC1 contains a logical contradiction: 'recovery that does NOT require remembering email' vs 'magic-link' (which inherently requires knowing the email to send the link). Forgotten-email lockout is fundamentally unsolvable without an alternate identifier (phone, admin lookup by name/kit) — the ticket must clarify whether the real ask is 'forgotten password with known email' (solvable) or 'forgotten email itself' (requires out-of-band admin search). Auth is blast-radius (org-scoped clarity-scout permission + kit_id gate, ScoutSetPasswordController:66-84 guards + email_verified_at one-shot, force-login via ScoutForceTokens). The scale is small (Scout is Pro-only, field-user subset), but auth changes touch login, token minting, middleware, and onboarding flows.

scope.summary: Keep Scout password auth. Add (1) self-serve Forgot Password on Login.vue that emails a 7-day relative signed reset link, (2) admin Reset Password action on ScoutUsersResource for verified users that emails the same style of link, (3) reset controller/routes that allow verified users (do not weaken onboarding one-shot). OTP/magic-link conversion out of scope.

questions.q: Does force-login (admin impersonation, ClarityScoutForceLoginController) satisfy AC2 'admin can assist recovery' or is a separate 'admin sends recovery email' action required? Force-login works but doesn't help a user log in themselves from the field.
questions.answer: Force-login is admin-only impersonation that requires the admin to be logged into Filament and have session('admin_impersonator') set (line 16). It does NOT help a Scout user in the field recover their own account — it's a diagnostic/support tool. AC2 requires a mechanism for the user to regain access themselves (email-delivered OTP or reset link), so a separate admin action is needed.

questions.q: AC1 says recovery without remembering email, but magic-link/OTP needs an email. What is the real lockout case?
questions.answer: Both: self-serve covers forgotten password with known email; forgotten email is admin lookup (name/kit) then assist using email on file.
options: Forgotten password (user still knows email) — OTP or reset link to that email
Forgotten email itself — admin finds the user (name/kit) and helps using the email on file
questions.pick: Forgotten password with known email is the self-serve case; forgotten email is admin lookup + assist. Both can be true, but self-serve cannot work without some identifier.

questions.q: Which auth recovery path ships in THIS ticket?
questions.answer: B — Keep passwords; add admin reset + Forgot Password email link (not OTP conversion in this ticket).
options: A — Convert Scout login to OTP/passwordless like Clarity (ticket preferred)
B — Keep passwords; add admin reset + optional Forgot Password email link
questions.pick: B first if we need the smallest fix for lockouts; A if product wants Scout aligned with Clarity now (larger change).

questions.q: If OTP (path A): replace password login entirely, or allow password OR OTP for a while?
questions.answer: N/A — skipped because path B (passwords kept).
questions.pick: OTP only — matches Clarity and avoids two login modes forever. Needs a clear cutover for existing Scout users.

questions.q: What should the admin action do when helping a locked-out Scout user?
questions.answer: A — Admin emails a recovery/reset link; user finishes on their device. Do not have admin set a temp password.
options: Email the user a recovery link or OTP (user finishes on their device)
Admin sets/tells them a temporary password (or reads an OTP over the phone)
questions.pick: Email a recovery link/OTP — safer and matches onboarding. Avoid admins setting passwords.

questions.q: Does Scout PWA need a self-serve Forgot Password / Request OTP on Login.vue, or is admin-only recovery enough?
questions.answer: A — Self-serve Forgot Password on Scout Login.vue, plus admin assist.
options: Self-serve on the login screen (plus admin assist)
questions.pick: Self-serve on login — AC1 asks for a recovery path; admin-only alone leaves field users stuck until an admin is free.

questions.q: If we keep signed reset/set-password links: reuse the 7-day TTL and one-shot rules, and should admin resend work for already-verified users?
questions.answer: A — Same 7-day relative signed URL pattern; new reset action for verified users; leave onboarding one-shot guard alone.
options: Yes — same 7-day signed link; new reset action works for verified users (onboarding resend stays unverified-only)
questions.pick: Same 7-day relative signed URL pattern (existing relative signed URLs); add a separate reset action for verified users. Do not remove the onboarding one-shot guard.
